searchText: More details on that. Client developers should fix me if I am wrong or missing anything Complexity that we currently have: * Pull blocks and deposit data from EL client via JSON-RPC * Keep the follow distance and cache the above data within the period Can be replaced with: * Have a logic that invalidates `Validator(pubkey, index)` cache entries on re-org -- potentially can be implemented in a couple of different ways We should think a bit more on what alternatives we do have but as for now it looks like a reasonable trade off The other option would be to track system deposits until finality, then apply them. we would have to queue them in some layer and take non-finality into account The CLs could queue them independently, then come to consensus on them along with finality (or the first block after finality or something). That is, we don't actually have to specify the mechanism for tracking them up until finality is reached. A client *could* choose to not track them at all and then when finality is achieved they could walk the chain backward. Potential problem with this: If the chain isn't finalizing, no new validators can join. The chain cannot receive new validators until *after* enough validators leak out and the chain starts finalizing again. You also have to update the validator client to handle indexes changing. Doable but it’s one example of how this is going to flow outward and show up in a few places. Block explorers would also be affected for example. Oh, yeah, it starts to leak into other pieces of client software 🤔 We may actually have a queue of deposits in the beacon state. Considering that deposit entry is more or less of the same data complexity as the validator entry, this may work, except for the case when deposit tops up the balance but not creating the new record. Though, I think topping up is much less frequent The problem of this scheme is requirement of seeking for *finalized* deposit index to drain the queue Mainnet-shadow-fork-12 merged ~1h ago, we used versions advertised in the EF blogpost. So far we've found 0 issues, there are no missed proposals, attestation rate didn't change pre-post merge and the network seems really stable. Great job to all the client teams!! 🎉 🚀 Niiiice! <n0ble> fantastic work everyone! oh yes, is this the last MSF? No, one more I think Yea, msf13 is already syncing :) I would guess it's the last one

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content:
More details on that. Client developers should fix me if I am wrong or missing anything
Complexity that we currently have: 
* Pull blocks and deposit data from EL client via JSON-RPC
* Keep the follow distance and cache the above data within the period
Can be replaced with:
* Have a logic that invalidates `Validator(pubkey, index)` cache entries on re-org -- potentially can be implemented in a couple of different ways

We should think a bit more on what alternatives we do have but as for now it looks like a reasonable trade off
